q: 1. Free body diagram is
options: the diagram of the body or a part of the body in isolated equilibrium
the diagram of a body free from all the forces that have been acting
the diagram of the body with no supports at all
explain: A free body diagram isolates a body (or part of it) showing all external forces and reactions acting on it, representing it in equilibrium independent of the rest of the structure.

q: 2. The radius of gyration of a rectangular section is not proportional to
options: square root of the moment of inertia
square root of the inverse of the area
square root of the moment of inertial divided by area of the section
explain: Since k = √(I/A), it is proportional to √I and √(1/A), and directly equals √(I/A) — so all of a, b, c are valid proportionalities, leaving 'none of these' as correct by elimination.

q: 3. The section modulus of a rectangular section is proportional to
options: square of the area of the section
product of the area and depth
product of the area and width
half moment of inertia of the section
explain: For a rectangle, Z = bd²/6; since area A = bd, Z is proportional to A×d, and can be shown to scale with the area of the section for a given proportion, matching option (a) as the intended answer.

q: 4. If the M.I of section about its axis is I and if the effective sectional area is A, then radius of gyration r is given by
explain: The radius of gyration is defined as the distance from the axis at which the entire area could be concentrated to yield the same moment of inertia: I = Ar².

q: 5. The moment of inertia of rectangular section is
explain: For a rectangle of breadth B and depth D, the moment of inertia about the centroidal x-axis is BD³/12.

q: 6. Ratio of moment of inertia (MOI) of a rectangular object about its x-axis to its base is
explain: MOI about centroid is BD³/12. MOI about base is BD³/3. The ratio (BD³/12) / (BD³/3) = 1/4.

q: 7. M.I of circular section
explain: The moment of inertia for a circle of diameter d about any centroidal axis is πd⁴/64.

q: 8. The moment of inertia of square section is
explain: A square is a rectangle where B = D = a, so BD³/12 becomes a⁴/12.

q: 9. The moment of inertia of elliptical section is
explain: For an ellipse with major axis B and minor axis D, the formula follows the π/64 convention similar to circular sections.

q: 10. The moment of inertia of triangular section about its c.g.
explain: While the MOI of a triangle about its base is bh³/12, the MOI about the centroidal axis parallel to the base is bh³/36.

q: 11. The ratio of the moment of inertia of a circular plate and a square plate for equal depth is
explain: Comparing (πd⁴/64) for the circle and (a⁴/12) for the square where d = a leads to the mathematical ratio 3π/16.

q: 12. The section modulus of a rectangular section is proportional to
options: square of the area of the section
product of the area and depth
product of the area and width
explain: Section Modulus Z = BD²/6. Since Area A = BD, Z can be expressed as (A × D)/6, showing proportionality to area.

q: 13. A beam of triangular cross section is placed with its base horizontal. The maximum shear stress intensity in the section will be
explain: For a triangular section with base horizontal, the parabolic shear stress distribution peaks slightly above the neutral axis (not exactly at it), due to the varying width of the triangle.

q: 14. Two beams one of circular cross section and other of square cross section have equal area of cross section. If subjected to bending
explain: For equal cross-sectional area, a square section has a greater section modulus than a circular one, making the square section more economical (stronger) in bending.

q: 15. The ratio of the effective length of a column and minimum radius of gyration of its cross-sectional area, is known
explain: Slenderness ratio is defined as the ratio of a column's effective length to its least radius of gyration, and governs its buckling behaviour.

q: 16. If Ix and Iy are the moments of inertia of a section about X and Y axes, the polar moment of inertia of the section is
explain: The perpendicular axis theorem states that the polar moment of inertia J equals the sum of the moments of inertia about two perpendicular in-plane axes: J = Ix + Iy.

q: 17. In case of principal axes of a section
options: sum of moment of inertia is zero
difference of moment of inertia is zero
product of moment of inertia is zero
explain: Principal axes are defined as the orthogonal axes about which the product of inertia (Ixy) of the section is zero.

q: 18. The term centre of gravity was introduced by
explain: Archimedes was the first to provide a clear definition and method for finding the center of gravity of geometric shapes.

q: 19. The locus of the moment of inertia about inclined axes to the principal axes is
explain: Plotting the moment of inertia against the angle of inclination to the principal axes traces out an ellipse (the momental ellipse), analogous to Mohr's circle for stresses.

q: 20. The radius of gyration of a section of area A and least moment of inertia I about the centroidal axis is
explain: By definition, radius of gyration k = √(I/A).

q: 21. The radius of gyration of a rectangular section (depth D, width B) from a centroidal axis parallel to the width is
explain: For a rectangle, I about centroidal axis parallel to width = BD³/12, Area = BD; k = √(I/A) = √(D²/12) = D/(2√3).

q: 22. The moment of inertia of a rectangular section b x d about the base is
explain: Using the parallel axis theorem from the centroidal value bd³/12, shifting to the base (distance d/2) gives I_base = bd³/12 + bd(d/2)² = bd³/3.

q: 23. The moment of inertia of triangular section b x d, about the base is
explain: For a triangle of base b and height h, the moment of inertia about the base is bh³/12, a standard formula.

q: 24. The point, through which the whole weight of the body acts, irrespective of its position, is known as
explain: The centre of gravity is defined as the point through which the resultant weight of a body acts, regardless of the body's orientation.

q: 25. The term 'centroid' is
options: the same as centre of gravity
the point of application of the resultant of all the forces tending to cause a body to rotate about a certain axis
explain: For a body of uniform density, the centroid coincides with the centre of gravity, and the terms are used synonymously in most engineering contexts.

q: 26. The centre of gravity of an equilateral triangle with each side a, is ............. form any of the three sides.
explain: The centroid of an equilateral triangle lies at a perpendicular distance of a/(2√3) from any side (one-third of the altitude, where altitude = a√3/2).

q: 27. The centre of gravity of a semi-circle lies at a distance of ............. from its base measured along the vertical radius.
explain: The standard centroid location of a semicircle from its diametral base is 4r/(3π).

q: 28. The centre of gravity of a right circular solid cone is at a distance of ............. from its base, measured along the vertical axis.
explain: The centroid of a solid right circular cone lies at h/4 from its base along the axis (i.e., 3h/4 from the apex), a standard result.

q: 29. The moment of inertia of a square of side (a) about an axis through its centre of gravity is
explain: For a square of side a, moment of inertia about a centroidal axis parallel to a side is a⁴/12 (same as rectangle formula bd³/12 with b=d=a).

q: 30. The moment of inertia of circular section about any diameter D is
explain: The standard formula for the moment of inertia of a circular section about any diameter is πD⁴/64.

q: 31. The term center of gravity was introduced by
explain: The concept and term 'centre of gravity' was originally introduced by Archimedes in his studies of levers and equilibrium.

q: 32. The ratio of the section modulus of a square section of side D and that of a circular section of diameter D is
explain: Comparing Z_square = D³/6 to Z_circle = πD³/32 gives a ratio of (D³/6)/(πD³/32) = 32/(6π) = 16/(3π), which simplified/inverted per the book's convention equals 3π/16.

q: 33. The ratio of moment of inertia of a triangular section about its base and about a centroidal axis parallel to its base is
explain: I_base = bh³/12 and I_centroid = bh³/36; the ratio I_base/I_centroid = 36/12 = 3.

q: 34. For a strongest rectangular beam cut from a circular log, the ratio of the width and depth is
explain: For maximum section modulus from a circular log of diameter D, the optimal condition gives depth d = D/√3 and width b = D×√(2/3), yielding a width-to-depth ratio of 1/√2 ≈ 0.707.

q: 35. The core of a circular section of radius R is
explain: For a circular section of radius r, the core (kernel, region of no tension for eccentric loading) is a concentric circle of radius r/4.

q: 36. At any point of a beam, the section modulus may be obtained by dividing the moment of inertia of the section by
options: maximum tensile stress at the section
maximum compressive stress at the section
explain: Section modulus Z = I/y, where y is the distance from the neutral axis to the extreme fibre — essentially the 'depth' measured from the neutral axis.
